packages.title: UK ETS maritime first scheme-year half-year QA
facts: The first UK ETS maritime scheme year runs from 1 July to 31 December 2026.
From 2027 the maritime scheme year runs from 1 January to 31 December.
The 2026 period is therefore a partial calendar year.
Annualised comparisons must preserve the shortened first scheme period.
The scheme period does not provide parcel emissions.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime gas-species scope QA
facts: UK ETS maritime monitoring covers carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide and methane.
Maritime emissions are expressed in carbon-dioxide equivalent for scheme purposes.
Gas-specific monitoring and CO2e totals are distinct representations.
Only maritime activities in scope of the scheme are included.
The operator-level scheme scope is not a land-parcel measurement.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime allowance surrender ratio QA
facts: For each tonne of CO2e in the maritime emissions figure for surrender, one UK allowance must be surrendered.
An allowance is a compliance unit rather than an emissions measurement.
The emissions figure for surrender can differ from gross maritime emissions where a permitted deduction applies.
Allowance holdings and market transactions are not themselves emissions.
No parcel value is inferred from allowance quantities.

packages.title: Maritime 2026 and 2027 surrender-deadline QA
facts: The surrender deadline for both the 2026 and 2027 maritime scheme years is 30 April 2028.
Later scheme years use the standard 30 April deadline following the scheme year.
Compliance deadlines must not be mistaken for emissions reference dates.
The 2026 and 2027 obligations remain separate scheme-year emissions figures.
A deadline is not an emissions value.

packages.title: Maritime emissions-monitoring-plan 42-day rule QA
facts: Maritime operators in scope must apply for an emissions monitoring plan within 42 days of a qualifying maritime activity.
The monitoring plan defines procedures, fuels, sources, factors and methods.
The plan is a compliance instrument rather than measured emissions itself.
Plan scope can change when ships, fuels or methods change.
No parcel emissions are inferred from plan existence.

packages.title: Maritime simplified monitoring voyage threshold QA
facts: Simplified monitoring can apply where a ship is scheduled for more than 300 voyages in the same scheme year and other conditions are met.
The simplified approach records annual fuel consumption instead of per-voyage fuel use.
It still requires fuel type, emission factors and total GHG emissions by gas type.
The voyage threshold is an eligibility criterion rather than an emissions threshold.
No parcel emissions value is produced.

packages.title: Maritime annual emissions report deadline QA
facts: Maritime annual emissions reports must be verified and submitted by 31 March following the scheme year.
The report must be accompanied by verification evidence.
Submission timing is separate from the emissions monitoring period.
Late submission can trigger regulator determination and penalties.
A submitted report is operator-level compliance evidence, not parcel evidence.

packages.title: Maritime annual-report ship fields QA
facts: The maritime annual emissions report includes total fuel consumed by fuel type for each ship.
It includes aggregated GHG emissions from in-port activities.
It includes aggregated GHG emissions for relevant voyages between UK ports.
Operator-level totals and eligible-fuel claims are also reported.
Aggregated ship and operator data must not be converted into land-parcel values.

packages.title: Maritime eligible-fuel emissions-reduction claim QA
facts: Eligible fuels meeting UK ETS claim rules can be treated with an emissions factor of zero for the approved claim.
A successful claim reduces the maritime emissions figure used for surrender.
The zero factor applies under the scheme claim rules rather than proving physical lifecycle zero emissions.
Supporting evidence and verification are required.
The claim cannot be used to infer parcel emissions.

packages.title: Maritime eligible-fuel no-double-counting QA
facts: A maritime eligible-fuel emissions-reduction claim requires a declaration of no double counting.
The fuel must not already have been used to obtain an emissions reduction or financial benefit in another scheme or scheme year.
Proof of purchase and delivery to a point of no return are required.
Fuel mass or volume and density evidence is also required.
Claim evidence is operator compliance evidence, not parcel data.

packages.title: Maritime independent verification QA
facts: All UK ETS maritime annual emissions reports require an independent verifier accredited by UKAS.
The verifier submits a verification report with the annual emissions report.
Verification is intended to provide assurance over monitored and reported emissions.
Verification does not make unrelated parcel values valid.
Verifier independence requirements must be preserved in provenance.

packages.title: Legacy UK maritime MRV revocation QA
facts: The previous UK maritime MRV instruments were revoked in April 2026 as UK ETS maritime monitoring replaced the prior regime.
Data up to the revocation period remains subject to the legacy verification arrangements described by MCA.
Old and new reporting regimes have different legal and operational boundaries.
Legacy MRV records must not be silently treated as UK ETS scheme-year records.
Neither regime provides land-parcel emissions by default.

packages.title: Energy Trends monthly two-month publication lag QA
facts: DESNZ monthly electricity tables ET 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5 are published with data two months in arrears.
They cover fuel use and generation by major power producers and electricity consumption.
Publication date and reference month therefore differ.
Monthly electricity activity statistics are not greenhouse-gas measurements by themselves.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from the lagged electricity tables.

packages.title: Energy Trends quarterly one-quarter lag QA
facts: DESNZ quarterly electricity tables are a quarter in arrears.
They cover fuel used, electricity generation, broad-sector consumption and interconnector imports and exports.
The tables include major power producers and other generators.
Reference period must be preserved separately from publication date.
Electricity-system activity is not parcel GHG measurement.

packages.title: EA pollution incidents category and closure scope QA
facts: The Environment Agency dataset includes substantiated completed and closed Environment Management incidents with category 1 or category 2 impact to at least one environmental medium.
Category 1 is major and category 2 is significant impact in the dataset description.
The dataset is predominantly pollution incidents.
Incident classification is not an emissions mass measurement.
A recorded incident does not create parcel GHG values.

packages.title: EA pollution-incident reporting lag QA
facts: The pollution-incident dataset is updated quarterly.
There is an inherent lag while incidents are investigated and records are completed.
Recent incidents may therefore be absent.
Records may change through final QA and additional information.
Absence from the snapshot does not prove absence of an incident or emissions.

packages.title: EA incident property-responsibility inference guard QA
facts: Environment Agency metadata warns that a recorded incident at a site or property does not imply the site or property owner was responsible.
Location and responsibility are separate concepts.
Incident data should not be used to assign liability without separate evidence.
Incident location is not a greenhouse-gas measurement.
No parcel responsibility or emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Pollution Inventory whole-permit point and fugitive scope QA
facts: The Environment Agency Pollution Inventory collates annual mass releases of specified substances to air, controlled waters and sewers and waste transfers from regulated industrial sites.
Reporting covers the whole permit or authorisation scope.
The scope includes point releases and non-point or fugitive releases.
Pollutant mass releases must remain distinct from waste-transfer quantities.
Facility or permit reporting is not automatically a cadastral parcel measurement.

packages.title: Industrial-emissions permit versus measured release QA
facts: Environment Agency 2026 IED collections publish permits, variations, surrenders and related regulatory decisions.
A permit issue or variation records regulatory status rather than an annual emissions amount.
Permit dates must not be treated as emissions reference periods.
Actual reported releases require separate Pollution Inventory or monitoring evidence.
A permit address does not justify inventing parcel GHG values.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel inference guard 109 QA
facts: Consumption footprints, agricultural inventories, maritime compliance records, electricity statistics, incident datasets and industrial permits use different measurement scopes.
National, sector, operator, facility and incident records cannot be arithmetically combined without compatible units, periods and boundaries.
Activity, compliance, permit and survey variables are not substitutes for measured parcel emissions.
No parcel binding has been executed in batch 109.
Measured parcel values produced remain zero.
